newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra looks to eliminate rail subsidies.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra looks to eliminate rail subsidies.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Wednesday would reform its loss-making Australian National rail business and perhaps eliminate the subsidies currently flowing into the operation.
Sharp issued a study showing that Australian National had lost A$135 million to A$148 million in the year to June 1996 and said the subisides would continue until a solution was found.
"And that solution hopefully will relieve us of, if not all of the subsidies, then certainly a major portion of the subsidies," he told reporters.
The report, by consultant John Brew, found that the operation had liabilities exceeding A$1 billion.

Part of this debt was accumulated financing assets that were transferred in 1993 to National Rail Corporation, an amalgam of the more profitable federal and state rail operations, including some split off from Australian National.
The result has been a collection of unprofitable operations in Australian National, which must also now compete with private rolling stock operators now allowed on the network.

Brew recommended further reorganisation of Australian National, including attempts to sell rail services or close them. "The financial and operational position of (Australian National) is extemely serious and deserves urgent consideration and action by the government," Brew said.
"The 1993 decision to transfer all interstate rail freight business from Australian National to National Rail Corporation made it almost impossible for Australian National to operate profitably."
Sharp said Cabinet would consider the issue.
